_note: The Structure view of the Economy section. 'today' figures are real data (CSO, 2025). 'design' ownership shares are the drafter's targets for the end of the transition (year 10), not findings: edit them freely. 'charter_today' is the approximate share of each sector's output produced by foreign multinationals, from the CSO's list of multinational-dominated industries; on the page it shrinks as the share of multinationals that leave rises in the pressure explorer.

tiers.governed: Boards one third elected by workers, one third by users and communities, one third appointed by the Executive with the Assembly's consent; accounts and plans published in full; hard budgets
Owned and run by county councils and local assemblies; capital budgets partly allocated by local assemblies (Art. 57)
One member, one vote; every worker admitted after at most a year's probation; non-members capped at a tenth of the workforce; reserves indivisible; may not be converted into a shareholder company
Up to fifty employees, and family farms of any size the law permits; a workplace council from twenty employees (Art. 34)
A published charter, approved by the Assembly, fixing tax, workers' rights, physical budgets and duties to train and share technology

free.note: Housing, health, care, childcare, education, public transport and a basic energy allowance (Q7)

planned.note: Investment in the major sectors is negotiated through the National Investment Council and approved by the Assembly and the Congress of Councils

market.note: Most consumer goods and everyday services are bought and sold freely, at prices set by the enterprises that make them

sectors.mode_note: Land use planned with farmers (Art. 67); food sold on markets
sectors.note: Family farms stay family farms (Art. 5.3, 51). Forestry stays with Coillte. Processing co-operatives are counted in industry

sectors.mode_note: Energy, water and major industry planned; much of manufacturing sells on markets
sectors.note: Electricity, gas networks, the grid and water are already State-owned (ESB, Gas Networks Ireland, EirGrid, Uisce Éireann). Dairy processing returns to farmer and worker co-operatives (Art. 67.3)

sectors.mode_note: Public housing and infrastructure planned; building work done by co-ops and small firms
sectors.note: Firms above fifty employees convert to co-operative or social ownership (Art. 47.2)
Large chains convert to consumer or worker co-operatives; shops, cafés and trades stay in private hands (Art. 51)

sectors.mode_note: Public transport free or at cost (Art. 24, 68); freight on markets
sectors.note: Irish Rail, Bus Éireann, Dublin Bus and the airports are already State-owned
Dominated today by foreign technology firms. Data centres are a designated sector for planned reduction (Art. 65, 114)

sectors.mode_note: Credit planned through the public bank network (Art. 61); housing provided at cost (Art. 69)
sectors.note: Public bank, credit unions (€22.5bn of assets today) and the Housing Authority
GVA covers legal, accounting and engineering services and administrative support only (other professional activities are not separately published)

sectors.mode_note: Free single-tier health service and National Care Service (Arts. 70, 71)
sectors.note: Includes care co-operatives within the National Care Service

sources.gva: CSO NA016, gross value added at basic prices, 2025, € billion (research 12 §2.1)
